headline: An AI-driven rush for capital gave Hong Kong its biggest summer of share sales on record, Bloomberg's data shows.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a record quarter confirmed with Bloomberg-compiled figures, but a market-data story rather than a single event.
importance_line: What changed is that Chinese AI companies are now raising money in Hong Kong repeatedly and in record sums, which affects ordinary investors buying into these deals, then the exchange and regulators watching deal quality, then the AI firms themselves, and the doubt is that Bloomberg notes rising bond yields and poor deal performance are already making buyers more cautious.
summary: Bloomberg reports that initial public offerings, placements and block trades in Hong Kong raised 47.5 billion dollars between July and September, the largest third quarter ever, pushing this year's total past 92 billion dollars and close to the 2021 record. AI companies drove it: Alibaba's 10.2 billion dollar share sale was the biggest deal, model maker Z.AI has raised 9.6 billion dollars this year across several offerings, and others returned to investors within months of listing, all while Asian stocks fell as much as 7 percent in July.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (403); full Bloomberg text read on The Edge Malaysia, which syndicates it. Linked to the Bloomberg original.
